t: You're at the site of Austin Friars, once an Augustinian friary in the City of London, from probably the 1260s until its dissolution in November 1538. It covered about five and a half acres, just north-east of the modern Bank of England, and was home to about sixty friars. A church stood at its centre, with buildings behind for living, eating and study, and large gardens grew vegetables, fruit and medicinal herbs. Edward of Angoulême, a child heir presumptive to the throne, is buried here. The astronomer Alexander Aubert was born here.
